newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Suspicious envelope addressed to U.N. press office.
newsitem.headline: Suspicious envelope addressed to U.N. press office.

text.p: Security guards closed off parts of the press area at U.N. headquarters Monday after the discovery of a suspicious envelope addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat, a U.N. spokesman said.
A letter bomb exploded earlier at the London office of the same newspaper, wounding two security guards. Four more suspect devices were found there later, British police said.
A U.N. source said mail delivered to the United Nations was scanned as a security precaution and this resulted in the discovery of the suspicious envelope.
Al-Hayat's office in Washington was the target of a letter bomb blitz in the United States earlier this month.
The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation is conducting an international investigation after eight letter bombs made to look like Christmas cards were mailed from Egypt to the United States.

None of the potentially lethal devices exploded. Five were addressed to Al-Hayat in Washington -- four arrived and one was found in the postal system -- and three turned up in the area around Leavenworth federal prison in Kansas.
